subject: Recap & next steps: NovusHealth qualification + bakeoff probe requests
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@novushealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps: NovusHealth qualification + bakeoff probe requests

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned: 

Pain points you emphasized:
- Unpredictable token costs on peak inference for high-concurrency workflows (claims summarization).
- Latency variance impacting batch SLA (tail latencies spike during EOD runs).
- Need for stronger audit logs and exportable KV-cache traces for troubleshooting.

Goals you shared:
- 99th percentile latency under 300ms for 1–2k QPS experimental load.
- <30% unit-cost reduction vs current baseline after basic batching + cache.
- SOC2-aligned evidence for a procurement checklist by the end of Q3.

Decision criteria you and Tom will use:
1) Latency consistency (P99 under threshold)
2) Cost per 1k tokens at target throughput
3) Integration effort for private deployment (VPC onboarding)
4) Observability: per-request token breakdown + KV visibility

Open questions / risks we flagged:
- Which models are in-scope for the bakeoff (open-source vs proprietary)?
- Expected sample payloads and peak concurrency windows (EOD batch vs realtime).
- Any firewall/VPN constraints for a short-lived private trial.

Proposed follow-ups (please confirm dates):
- Novus provides representative sample payloads and a short list of 3 models you want tested (due Fri 8/22).
- Redwood runs two targeted probe sprints: 1) latency-focused (P99 & tail) and 2) cost-focused (batching/quant profiles) — results by Wed 8/28.
- Live 60-min bakeoff demo + deep-dive on 8/29 or 8/30 (you pick).

Attachments I’m including: our probe sprint template (redwood-probe-sprint-template.pdf) and a blank vendor matrix to capture your internal weights (novus_bakeoff_criteria.xlsx).

If that all looks right, can you confirm the models and a preferred date for the bakeoff demo? Also please loop procurement when you’re ready so we can prep the trial paperwork.

Thanks —

Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-probe-sprint-template.pdf]
[Attachment: novus_bakeoff_criteria.xlsx]

From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@novushealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@novushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Aug 2025 09:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: NovusHealth qualification + bakeoff probe requests

Logan —

Appreciate the clear recap — this aligns with our notes. Quick answers: 

- Models: we want to test two open models (Llama3-13b Q8 and Mistral-7B) and one hosted variant (vendor-managed 13b) to evaluate both self-host and hosted options.
- Sample payloads: attaching a small sample set (500 records) we anonymized for the bakeoff — contains typical claims text and metadata columns.
- Peak windows: main concern is EOD batch between 01:00–03:00 local time and a steady realtime stream during business hours (~150–250 RPS).

Procurement: I’ve added procurement@novushealth.com to the thread. They’ll need the SOC2 artifacts and a high-level SOW before trial onboarding.

Proposed bakeoff demo date: 8/29 works best for Tom and me. If you can do results by 8/28, we’ll review internally on 8/29 and ask questions live.

Attachments: novus_sample_payloads.csv (sample), internal_weighting_short.docx (Tom’s scoring suggestion).

Thanks,
Sarah Lim
Sr. Product Manager — Data Insights
NovusHealth
[Attachment: novus_sample_payloads.csv]
[Attachment: internal_weighting_short.docx]

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@novushealth.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: NovusHealth qualification + bakeoff probe requests

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for sending the payloads and the model shortlist — these are perfect. Couple of notes from an engineering/testing perspective and the test plan I’ll run once we receive confirmation: 

Planned probe sprint (high level):
- Sprint A (Latency): run 3x 30-min ramp tests across the three model variants with synthetic concurrency matching EOD windows; capture P50/P95/P99, token breakdown, and KV-cache hit rates.
- Sprint B (Cost): use continuous batching profiles + quantized weights (Q8) where available and measure cost-per-1k tokens at 3 throughput points.
- Observability checks: verify per-request token usage and KV exports; snapshot export for SOC artifact checklist.

Data/practical asks from Novus to speed things up:
1) Confirm sample payload folder path in Drive (we have read access?) or we can pull from the attached CSV.
2) Any IP ranges for a short-lived VPC trial so we can pre-authorize endpoints.
3) If you have a priority weighting for criteria (latency vs cost vs integration), share it — we’ll use it to produce a scored vendor matrix.

I attached a short vendor-capacity matrix CSV we use to score throughput/latency tradeoffs; please review when you have a minute.

We’ll target delivering the sprint A results by EOD 8/26 and sprint B by 8/28, which should let us debrief live on 8/29.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: vendor-capacity-matrix.csv]
